name: @recoder/connectors
description: Recoder's connectors / social-gateway package — owned in place from OpenClaw's extracted gateway-core + social-gateways + embedded agents. Foundation: the ConnectorPort contract, connector domain types, the connector trust boundary (allowlist + mention + command gating), and the embedded-agent auth/runner contracts. Per-channel adapters (telegram/slack/discord/signal/line/feishu/imessage/whatsapp) wrap each real gateway behind ConnectorPort.
author: Recoder (recoder.xyz)
//exports: Subpaths ./telegram ./slack ./signal ./imessage ./whatsapp ./line ./feishu ./discord are the typecheck-clean per-channel ConnectorPort adapters; each is its own entry so importing one pulls only that channel's optional SDK. All eight are wired live end-to-end and proven by per-channel dispatch tests (social-gateways/_dispatch/*.dispatch.test.ts) that route a real channel-native event through the adapter's REAL normalize + REAL send (gate -> embedded runner -> port.send) doubling only each channel's true SDK seam. The Discord adapter (./discord) is the social-gateways/discord/connector/ slice: a real, self-contained ConnectorPort over the Discord REST v10 wire surface (fetch is its SDK seam) that composes its own normalize / send / chunk / accounts and imports NOTHING from the un-extracted OpenClaw bot core (auto-reply/*, channels/*, gateway/*, pairing/*, security/*, config/*, routing/*, web/media, polls, markdown/*, agents/identity, logger/logging). The legacy bot-core-coupled discord siblings (../send.ts, ../normalize.ts, ../targets.ts, ../accounts.ts, ../token.ts, ../chunk.ts) are left untouched as reference source and are NOT entry points.
//peerDependencies: Channel SDKs are loaded by the per-channel adapter phase (not the foundation). The foundation src/ imports none of them, keeping install ENOSPC-safe on the disk-constrained dev box. The real, working gateway source under social-gateways/* uses these; they are declared optional so adapters can pull them in without a root-workspace install.
